program: Business English — Corporate Communication in a Global Airline
hub_subtitle: Reunião regional, e-mail corporativo, treinamento global e convenção internacional

lesson.menu_title: It Was Launched Last Year — The Language of the Announcement
lesson.menu_desc: The passive voice, and what it hides when a company writes about itself -- 36 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- It Was Launched Last Year
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 9 -- It Was Launched Last Year

listenings.text: Good morning. This is the quarterly commercial announcement, and it is being sent to all commercial teams in the four countries. Three items. First, the regional office in Bogota has been fully staffed as of last week, and the remaining two positions were filled internally. Second, the new booking platform will be rolled out in March, and training sessions are going to be scheduled for every account manager before that date. Attendance is required. Third, the corporate fare structure has been revised. Existing contracts are not affected, and clients will be informed by their account manager, not by a central email. That last point is important. Nobody should hear this from a system.

Something I have learned about corporate writing, and I wish somebody had told me twenty years earlier. When you read a company announcement, ask one question of every sentence: who did this? Half the time the answer is right there. The other half, the sentence has been built so that the answer is missing. Mistakes were made. The decision was taken. The position has been eliminated. Nobody is lying, and often there is a good reason to leave the person out. But if you are the one writing, be careful. The passive is a wonderful tool for describing a process and a terrible way to deliver bad news, because the person receiving it always hears the same thing: somebody did this to me, and you will not say who.

items.situation: You have to tell a client that the fare structure changed, without blaming a colleague.
tips: The passive removes the person, and here that is fair
The fare structure has been revised

items.situation: Your director asks who approved the discount.
tips: Here the active is the honest answer
Compliance approved it on Tuesday -- do not hide behind was approved

items.situation: You are describing the new booking platform to a client.
tips: A process takes the passive naturally
It will be rolled out in March and everybody will be trained first

items.situation: You have to tell a colleague his request was refused.
tips: Do not deliver bad news in the passive
Say who decided and why, in one sentence

items.situation: A client asks whether his contract is affected.
tips: Existing contracts are not affected -- I will call you if that changes

items.situation: Somebody asks when the office was opened.
tips: Past passive: was plus the third form
It was opened in September, and it has been fully staffed since last week

extra_audio.text: Felipe says the quarterly announcement has been sent to all four countries and asks whether Rosa has read it. Rosa answers that she has read it twice and that one sentence is not clear. Felipe asks which sentence, and Rosa quotes the line about the fare structure being revised. Felipe explains who actually took the decision and why the announcement does not say so. Rosa says she will call her clients herself instead of letting them read it in a central email.
